units.description: This theme covers the identified gaps in drainage research where additional field data, experimental studies across diverse soils and climates, and empirical estimates are needed to validate and verify models and hypotheses related to water balance, preferential flow, and nutrient transport in tile-drained systems.

units.theme: Subsurface Drainage Flow Modeling Research Gaps
units.description: This theme covers identified gaps and future research priorities in understanding and modeling water movement in subsurface drainage systems, including preferential flow characterization across varying soil and management conditions. It emphasizes the need for coupled surface-subsurface hydraulic models and long-term monitoring to validate and improve drainage design recommendations.

units.theme: Future Research and Management Practices Needed
units.description: This theme addresses gaps in current knowledge and practice, emphasizing the need for further research to identify cost-effective nutrient mitigation strategies and improved cropping practices, while also highlighting alternative edge-of-field and agronomic approaches to reduce nutrient losses from tile-drained agricultural landscapes.

units.theme: Future Research Needs for Crop-Drainage Systems
units.description: This theme covers recommended next steps in field experiments and modeling studies to better understand how crop yield, nitrogen losses, and water balance respond to varying soils, climates, cover crops, and drainage management practices. The statements collectively call for expanded empirical and simulation work across diverse agronomic and hydrological conditions in tile-drained agricultural systems.

This theme covers research gaps and practical strategies for reducing nitrate-N losses to subsurface drainage water and groundwater. It encompasses calls for further field experiments on cover crops and on-farm drainage systems, as well as specific N management adjustments—such as crediting residual soil NO3-N, refining yield goals, and adapting applications to soil and weather conditions—to minimize leaching.

This theme covers knowledge gaps and future research needs related to field bioreactor sizing and performance, specifically evaluating undersized bioreactors, scaling designs for flashy drainage sites, and understanding contaminant transport (nitrate, phosphorus, pesticides) through drainage inlets.

This theme covers the need to test and validate tile-drainage models using additional field data spanning varied spatial scales, soil types, and longer time periods. The statements collectively emphasize that broader empirical testing is required to confirm model robustness and parameter reliability across different regions and conditions.

units.theme: Controlled Drainage and Irrigation Water Management
units.description: This theme covers the integration of controlled drainage systems with irrigation practices to optimize agricultural water use. It addresses expanding farmer control options within drainage systems, coordinating drainage and irrigation adjustments, and ongoing research to refine these techniques.

This theme covers the need to refine, calibrate, and validate watershed hydrological models to assess the impacts of drainage water management practices on nutrient cycling. It also encompasses recommendations for large-scale modeling efforts to prioritize drainage water management implementation and calls for expanding research to less intensely drained watersheds.

units.theme: Long-Term Organic Soil Drainage Research Gaps
units.description: This theme covers identified gaps and methodological recommendations for studying nutrient (N and P) losses and water balance in drained organic soils. The statements collectively call for extended multi-year studies, improved P saturation metrics, and isotope-based tracing approaches to better understand loss pathways and nutrient dynamics in these systems.

This theme covers the recognized need for extended, ongoing monitoring and additional empirical measurements in tile drainage research. The statements collectively emphasize that current findings are preliminary and that further data collection across multiple scales and timeframes is required before firm conclusions can be drawn.

units.theme: Tile Drainage Research Gaps and Modeling Needs
units.description: This theme covers identified limitations and future directions in tile drainage research, including the need for improved watershed-scale hydrologic modeling with field verification, better accounting of manure, soil types, and nutrient loadings at various reach scales, and careful consideration of tile flow parameter uncertainty when drainage specifications are unknown during model calibration.

units.theme: Subsurface Drainage for Soil Salt Leaching
units.description: This theme addresses knowledge gaps and monitoring needs related to how subsurface tile drainage removes salts from soil and water over time. The statements collectively highlight that long-term observation, surface water monitoring, and extended drainage periods are required to fully understand and detect salt reduction outcomes.

units.theme: Bioaugmentation to Enhance Woodchip Bioreactor Denitrification
units.description: This theme covers the potential of inoculating denitrifying microorganisms (bioaugmentation) into woodchip bioreactors to improve nitrate removal, particularly under low-temperature and field conditions. The statements highlight that further research is needed to confirm whether these denitrifiers can effectively reduce nitrate to N2 within woodchip bioreactor environments.
